title: Artemis-N3DS: Streaming games to a Nintendo 3DS

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Picture a Nintendo 3DS, a little handheld with two screens, playing a PC game streamed live over Wi-Fi. That's what this project is about.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Wait, a console from that era handling a sixty frames per second stream? How?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Antoine's repository is a fork of Moonlight Embedded, adapted to the whole Nintendo 3DS family. Moonlight is the open streaming client, and this version teaches it to speak 3DS.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So what does the adapting actually cover?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Four things. It finds the host computer on the network and pairs with it, it gives the console its own interface, it handles the buttons and touch input, and it shows the video across that dual-screen hardware. The newer New 3DS gets its own hardware path.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I like that it's framed as constrained systems engineering. Small ARM chip, modest Wi-Fi, and still a smooth picture.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. And the code is mostly C plus plus, with a Docker option for building it, and the upstream project is properly credited.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The written page has the details on the build setup and the modules.
